# H004 — No protein-coding gene outside the eight-gene panel carries a candidate biallelic set of rare protein-altering PASS alleles that outranks the BUB1B pair: BUB1B is the only gene that is biallelic on PASS calls AND carries a ClinVar pathogenic allele AND sits in the top 30 of the panel-blind phenotype ranking.

**Step:** [step-2](../README.md) — Which variants are rare enough and damaging enough to cause an ultra-rare recessive disease, and in which gene?
**Status:** supported  |  **Confidence:** 0.93  |  **Revisions:** 2
**Gene:** BUB1B  |  **Path:** path 1 — textbook clinic, genome-wide

## The claim

No protein-coding gene outside the eight-gene panel carries a candidate biallelic set of rare protein-altering PASS alleles that outranks the BUB1B pair: BUB1B is the only gene that is biallelic on PASS calls AND carries a ClinVar pathogenic allele AND sits in the top 30 of the panel-blind phenotype ranking.

**Prediction if true.** In results.gene_biallelic (every coding allele genome-wide annotated by VEP REST), BUB1B is flagged biallelic_pass with n_plp_pass >= 1 and phenotype_rank <= 30, and no other gene satisfies all three conditions at once. Other genes with biallelic_pass true will exist (recessive carriers of two rare missense alleles are common in any genome) but none will combine a pathogenic ClinVar allele with a phenotype rank in the top 30.

**What would refute it.** Another gene with biallelic_pass true, at least one ClinVar pathogenic or LoF allele, and a phenotype rank of 30 or better; or BUB1B failing to appear as biallelic_pass in the genome-wide table (which would mean the coding-region join or the annotation lost one of its alleles).

## Evidence

| # | Direction | Strength | Kind | Observation | Source |
|---|---|---|---|---|---|
| 12 | supports | 0.80 | measurement | Genome-wide coding scan (38,087 distinct coding alleles, all annotated by VEP REST release 116): 667 genes carry at least one rare protein-altering allele, 65 are biallelic on PASS calls, and exactly one of the 65 carries a ClinVar pathogenic allele - BUB1B, which is also the only biallelic gene with a phenotype rank of 30 or better (rank 6). | `methodology/070` |
| 13 | supports | 0.50 | measurement | Of the 15 biallelic genes carrying a loss-of-function allele, none other than BUB1B has a ClinVar pathogenic allele, and their phenotype ranks are 220 or worse or absent; the biallelic set outside BUB1B is dominated by HLA genes, SERPINA1 and other hypervariable or paralogous loci - the shape of mapping noise and common recessive carrier states, not of a second diagnosis. | `methodology/070` |
| 14 | neutral | 0.00 | absence | The scan covers coding intervals plus an 8 bp splice flank only (1.4 percent of the genome); a deep-intronic, UTR or structural second allele in another gene is outside what this test can see, so the verdict is a statement about the coding fraction. | `methodology/070` |
